units: <cite ref="Chullin 8a:1">Ḥull. 8ᵃ</cite> <he>והאיכא צ׳</he> but are there not the sides (of the heated knife which burn instead of cutting)? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 13:7:3">Y. Sabb. XIII, end, 14ᵇ</cite> <he>צִידְדֵי בהמה</he> the sides of a beast. Bab.
<cite ref="Shabbat 154b:17">Sabb. 154ᵇ</cite> <he>צ׳ הן וצ׳ לא וכ׳</he> this is making use of the sides of a beast, and this the Rabbis have not forbidden.
<cite ref="Shabbat 154b:17">Ib.</cite> <he>צִדְדֵי צ׳</he> the sides of sides, indirect use of the sides of an object (v. <cite ref="R00078"><he>צַד</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 126:1">Sifré Num. 126</cite> <he>בכל צְדָדָיו</he> on any of its sides, opp. entrance of the tent.
<cite ref="Shabbat 6a:16">Sabb. 6ᵃ</cite> <he>צִדֵּי רשות הרבים</he> the sides (the walls &c.) along the public road.
<cite ref="Shabbat 99a:4">Ib. 99ᵃ</cite> <he>צידי עגלה</he> the sides of a wagon; <he>עגלות תחתיהן וביניהן וצִידֵּיהֶן</he> the spaces under wagons and between them, and their outsides.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 6:2:6">Y. Peah VI, 19ᶜ</cite> top <he>דבר שהוא חומר משני צ׳</he> where a rule works as a restriction both ways; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 16b">B. Kam. 16ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>לצ׳ קתני</he> it is meant in either way, i.e. disjunctively, the one or the other. Y. Yeb. IV, 5ᵈ <he>לצ׳ … או וכ׳</he> the Mishnah means the Vav in a disjunctive sense, ‘or’ &c.
